mini-app.name: mini-app
mini-app.about: 292 lines of untyped TypeScript with 17 tests, written to measure ts-capture against types a person wrote first.

nest.name: nestjs/nest
nest.about: The NestJS framework, at a pinned commit, observed through its own test suite.

hono.name: honojs/hono
hono.about: The Hono web framework, at a pinned commit, observed through its own test suite. Already strictly typed: there is little left to add.

examples.title: Parameters and a return type, from the calls the tests made
examples.caption: Every test passed a number and got a number back. Some passed a coupon and some passed none, so the parameter is the coupon's shape or undefined.

examples.title: A callback, typed from what it returned
examples.caption: The tests hand the service a function that returns a Date. ts-capture saw it called and saw what came back. gateway stays as it was: what was observed of it carried nothing worth writing.

examples.title: An element of a collection TypeScript knows nothing about
examples.caption: cart is still any, so TypeScript has no type for line. The observed shape is all there is, and it is written on the callback and on the result.

examples.title: Keys that came from the test data
examples.caption: The return type lists the two SKUs the tests used. The function accepts any SKU: it indexes by a variable. Nothing flags this, because the type describes the test run exactly.

examples.title: A lookup that can miss, typed as if it always hits
examples.caption: Map.get returns undefined for an unknown id. Every test asked for an order that existed, so undefined was never observed.

examples.title: A position it observed and did not write
examples.caption: threshold is written; stock is not. The observed shape would have added a type error on the next line, so apply left the parameter as it was and said so in its report.

leftAlone.name: stock
leftAlone.reason: TS7053 at src/inventory.ts:10: Element implicitly has an 'any' type because expression of type 'string' can't be used to index type '{ "sku-chair": number; "sku-lamp": number; }'.   No index signature with a parameter of type 'stri…

examples.title: A type that already has a name
examples.caption: The observed object matches a type that is in scope, so the annotation is that name and not the shape spelled out.

examples.title: A union of what actually flowed through
examples.caption: Across the tests this held a string, an array of strings, and undefined. The annotation is the three together.

examples.title: Test data in a real project
examples.caption: The collection holds whatever metadata a caller attached. both and only2 are keys from nest's own tests, now written into the source as if they were the type.
examples.better: leave it unannotated, or type the collection where it is built

examples.title: A callback's return type, by name
examples.caption: The parameter was typed already. What the callback returned matched RouteData, a type the file already uses, so that name is written and not the shape.

examples.title: A disagreement, reported and not written
examples.caption: In the tests cache.match gave null, where TypeScript infers Response or undefined. ts-capture does not write a type the checker contradicts. It leaves a note saying what it saw.

examples.title: The wrapper object, not the primitive
examples.caption: Hono's escaped strings are String objects, and that is what was observed. The annotation is accurate about the value and is not the type the code means.
examples.after:
const callbacks = htmlArray
              .map((html: String) => (html as HtmlEscapedString).callbacks || [])
              .flat()
